# Detailed weighted Poisson estimates {#sec-appendix-poisson}

For completeness, we account for every line in @eq-weighted-poisson.  Work first up to the exit time $\tau_K$ from a compact parameter region.  By the locally uniform geometric drift and minorization properties, and after enlarging $K$ slightly if necessary, stopped expectations of $V(X_k)$ are uniformly bounded.  The same bounds apply to $V^{2\beta}(X_k)$, since $2\beta\leq1$.

**Martingale.**  From @eq-poisson-lipschitz and conditional Jensen's inequality,

$$
\mathbb E\!\left[\|M_k\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\tau_K\geq k\}}\right]
\leq C_K\,\mathbb E[
V^{2\beta}(X_{k-1})+V^{2\beta}(X_k);
\tau_K\geq k]\leq C_K.
$$ {#eq-martingale-bound}

Thus $\sum_k\gamma_kM_k\mathbf1_{\{\tau_K\geq k\}}$ is an $L^2$-bounded martingale, and the martingale convergence theorem makes its tails vanish uniformly over their terminal index.

**Endpoints.**  Markov's inequality and @eq-poisson-lipschitz give

$$
\sum_k\mathbb P\left(
\gamma_k\|v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_{k-1})\|>\varepsilon,\,
\tau_K\geq k\right)
\leq \varepsilon^{-2}C_K\sum_k\gamma_k^2<\infty.
$$ {#eq-endpoint-bound}

Hence $\gamma_kv_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_{k-1})\to0$ almost surely on the localized event, by Borel--Cantelli.  The two endpoint contributions therefore vanish even when the upper index $m$ varies.

**Step-size variation.**  Because $(\gamma_k)$ is nonincreasing and converges to zero,

$$
\sum_{k=1}^\infty|\gamma_{k+1}-\gamma_k|
=\gamma_1<\infty.
$$

Since $\mathbb E[V^\beta(X_k);\tau_K\geq k]\leq C_K$, the expectation of the absolute sum
$\sum|\gamma_{k+1}-\gamma_k|\|v_{\theta_k}(X_k)\|$ is finite.  Thus that sum converges almost surely.

**Parameter variation.**  Use the exact place where the parameter increments enter:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_k\|v_{\theta_k}(X_k)-v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_k)\|
&\leq L_K\gamma_k\|\theta_k-\theta_{k-1}\|V^\beta(X_k)\\
&\leq C_K\gamma_k^2V^{2\beta}(X_k).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-moving-poisson-bound}

The sum of the right-hand side has finite expectation on the stopped process.  This is a bound for differences of the **Poisson solution evaluated at successive parameters**, rather than a bound for a general extra error in the SA recursion.

The four convergent expressions prove @eq-noise-tail by passing to their tails.  Taking a countable compact exhaustion and ignoring a finite initial segment transfers the localized claim to every eventually compact trajectory.
